sentences.text: Heard on I.A.No.32954 of 2024 which is bail application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C. for suspension of remaining jail sentence and grant of bail to appellant No.2 Shailendra @ Rinku.

The appellant No.2 has been convicted under Section 366-A of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I.
for ten years and fine of Rs.1,000/- , under Section 376 DA of the IPC sentenced to undergo R.I. for life imprisonment and fine of Rs.3,000/-, under Section 370A of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I.
for ten years and fine of Rs.1,000/-, under Section 368 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for ten years and fine of Rs.1,000/- and under Section 5(g)/6,5(l)/6,5(j)(ii)/6 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for twenty years and fine of Rs.2,000/- with default stipulations.
Learned counsel for the appellant No.2 submits that co-accused persons namely Rohit Sharma @
Chotu, Vivek @ Tillu, Deependra Sharma @ Dipu and Rishab Sharma @ Rishu have been granted bail by this Court vide orders dated 09.09.2024 and 25.10.2024 and case of present appellant is almost identical to that of aforesaid appellants.

After referring to evidence of 2 CRA-2882-2023 prosecutrix's father (PW-3) and Laxmi Patel (PW-5) (Assistant teacher), it is urged that in the instant case, from evidence on record, it is not established that prosecutrix was minor on the date of incident.
No documents pertaining to date of birth of prosecutrix are proved to have been submitted in the school at the time of admission.

Further, after referring to deposition of prosecutrix as well as her brother, it is urged that earlier also, prosecutrix had levelled same allegations against other persons and aforesaid matters have been reported stating that at the time of incident, prosecutrix was minor.
It is also urged that appellant has served sentence of more than four years.
This appeal is of year 2023.
Early hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future.
On above grounds, it is urged that jail sentence of appellant No.2 be suspended and he be released on bail.

sentences.text: Learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State, on the other hand, has opposed the application.
Having regard to evidence available on record, especially, deposition of prosecutrix, we deem it proper to suspend the sentence and release appellant No.2 on bail.
Accordingly, I.A.No.32954 of 2024 is allowed.

Subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant No.2 is hereby suspended and it is directed that the appellant No.2 be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court with a further direction to appear before the concerning trial court on 07.04.2025 and also on such other dates, as may be fixed by the trial court in this regard 3 CRA-2882-2023 during the pendency of this appeal.
List the case for final hearing in due course.
C. c. as per rules.

(SANJAY DWIVEDI) (ACHAL KUMAR  JUDGE JUDG  vai Smt. Anuradha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171337395/
